# Kaya of the Canopy

An original 2D jungle platformer in the spirit of early-90s DOS action games:
16×16 tiles, screen-flip scrolling, an overworld hub, animal transformations and
a boomerang blade. Design source: `jungle-platformer-plan.md`.

**All assets are original.** Art and audio are *generated by scripts in `tools/`*,
not copied from anywhere. Never add third-party sprites, music or level data.

## Stack
Godot 4.7 (GL Compatibility renderer), GDScript. Logical resolution **400×240**,
integer-scaled, nearest-neighbour. Fixed 60 Hz sim in `_physics_process`.

## Commands
All scripts read `tools/env.sh` for the local Godot and Python paths. That file
is gitignored — copy `tools/env.sh.example` and edit it after a fresh clone.

- Run tests: `tools/test.sh`  (headless; non-zero exit on failure)
- Validate scenes/levels: `tools/validate.sh`
- Re-import assets after regenerating art: `tools/import.sh`
- Regenerate art: `tools/genart.sh`
- Regenerate audio: `tools/genaudio.sh`
- Screenshot the running game: `tools/shot.sh --scenario=title --out=shots/x.png`
  or `tools/shot.sh --seq=tools/seq/<name>.json` for scripted play
- Upscale a capture for review: `tools/upscale.sh shots/x.png shots/x3.png 3`
- Contact-sheet several captures: `tools/grid.sh out.png <cols> <scale> a.png b.png …`
- In-game integration suite: `tools/itest.sh` (needs a display; hard-bounded)
- Rebuild levels from the authoring DSL: `tools/genlevels.sh`
- Export: `tools/export_web.sh` / `export_macos.sh` / `export_android.sh` /
  `export_ios.sh` / `export_playtest.sh` — see `docs/shipping.md`
- Smoke-test an exported build: `tools/smoke_build.sh`

## Conventions
- **No engine physics for gameplay.** All movement goes through
  `src/world/tile_collision.gd` (static, pure) against a `TileWorld`.
- Positions are floats; only rendering rounds to whole pixels.
- Speeds are px/s, accelerations px/s². Never a magic number in a script —
  tunables live in `data/` (`forms/*.json`, `enemies/*.json`, `weapons/*.json`).
- Game code never reads `Input` directly; it reads an `InputState`.
- Scenes are text `.tscn`, kept small and mostly built from code, because the
  editor is not part of the loop. Node names PascalCase, files snake_case.
- Levels are `levels/*.json` (see `docs/adr/002-level-format.md`).
- GDScript is compiled with warnings-as-errors: annotate anything inferred from
  a Variant (`round()`, ternaries, `Dictionary` reads) with an explicit type.

## Testing has two tiers (ADR 003)
`--headless --script` has **no autoloads and no scene tree**, so:
- `tools/test.sh` covers pure logic and data (collision, level parsing, form
  maths, asset presence).
- `tools/itest.sh` boots the real game and drives it frame by frame — anything
  built out of nodes (blade, enemies, pickups, triggers, pause, touch) is
  verified there, in `levels/test_arena.json`.

Neither tier can see a packaging mistake, which is what `tools/smoke_build.sh`
is for.

## Definition of done for a task
1. `tools/test.sh` passes.
2. `tools/validate.sh` passes.
3. `tools/itest.sh` passes if the change touches anything with a node.
4. A screenshot in `shots/` proves the feature renders.
5. `CHANGELOG.md` mentions the change.
